message:
Merge production-hardened & Next.js 15 release into main

Consolidate the fully audited, Next.js 15 upgraded codebase as the
authoritative main branch. Supersedes the previous main content.

chore(deps): upgrade to Next.js 15.5.20 and migrate async request APIs

- Bump next 14.2.35 -> 15.5.20, eslint-config-next & @next/bundle-analyzer to ^15
- Await async dynamic APIs and route inputs (Next 15 breaking changes):
  - headers() is now async in layout.tsx / products page
  - route params are now Promise (comments [id], replies, replies/[replyId])
  - page searchParams are now Promise (home, about, products)
- Remove NextRequest.ip (removed in Next 15); derive client IP from
  x-real-ip / x-forwarded-for proxy headers in comments auth
- Tighten route handler context typing to match the strict generated
  .next/types RouteContext (drop | undefined on second handler arg;
  withRequestLogging now propagates a non-optional context)
- Fix latent bug: await deleteStoredReply in DELETE replies route
  (Promise was always truthy, so 404 branch was unreachable)
- Update contact route tests to pass explicit context argument

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean (incl. generated route types),
npm test 49/49 pass, gitleaks no leaks, next build compiles.
High-severity Next.js DoS advisory resolved by 15.5.20.

chore(deps): remove junk/unused deps, patch Next, fix transitive CVEs

Supply-chain hygiene (Phase 7):
- Remove `docker@1.0.0`: not Docker at all but an abandoned 2015 'docco'
  documentation generator, never imported — a dependency-confusion /
  accidental install. Its tree carried 6 critical + many high CVEs.
- Remove `chromedriver`: unused. Playwright manages its own Chromium
  (see scripts/ensure-chromium.mjs); the standalone driver only added
  attack surface.
- `npm audit fix` (non-breaking) for transitive advisories (ws, yaml,
  postcss, etc.).
- Bump next / eslint-config-next / @next/bundle-analyzer 14.2.33 -> 14.2.35
  (latest patch in the 14.2.x line; no breaking changes).

Result: npm audit 60 -> 22 total, prod-only 28 -> 2. Remaining 2 prod
advisories are Next.js issues fixed only in 15.x/16.x (breaking major),
intentionally deferred to a dedicated upgrade with full regression
testing. Build (next 14.2.35) compiles; tsc clean; 49/49 tests pass.

docs(middleware): replace decorative author note with CSP rationale

Line 51 carried a leftover Persian author marker ('only the real change
happened here') with no technical meaning. Replace it with a comment
explaining why styleSrc differs between dev (unsafe-inline for HMR) and
production (nonce-pinned).

fix(env): stop fabricating placeholder values for URL/connection vars

The build-time env fallback injected a synthetic `auto-<key>-<rand>`
value for every missing recommended variable. For connection-string /
URL keys this was actively harmful: the storage layer treats
COMMENTS_DATABASE_URL/DATABASE_URL as a SQLite file path, so the bogus
value produced stray `auto-comments_database_url-*` (+ -wal/-shm)
database files in the working directory on every lint/test/dev build,
and would fail the new Zod connection-URL validation.

These keys are all 'recommended' (never required), so leaving them
unset is safe — db.ts falls back to the default SQLite path / read-only
guard and the rate limiter falls back to its in-memory store. Only
presence-check them; never fabricate a fake connection string.

security(P1): constant-time compare for admin session key

The admin-session issuance route compared the provided session key to
the configured secret with a plain `!==`, which short-circuits on the
first differing byte and leaks key-prefix length via response timing.
Reuse the existing HMAC-grade timingSafeEqual (now exported) so session
minting is not distinguishable by a timing side channel.

Adds auth.test.ts covering timingSafeEqual edge cases (equal, unequal,
length-mismatch, empty) and signed-session round-trip / missing-secret.

ci(secret-scan): allowlist synthetic test fixtures in gitleaks rule

The comments-admin-token rule flagged the deterministic fixture value
used by app/lib/env-schema.test.ts. Test fixtures are not real
credentials, so allowlist them narrowly (fixture regex + *.test.ts
path scope) rather than weakening the detection regex.

feat(env): add Zod value-level validation with production fail-fast

The existing env layer only checked variable *presence*. A malformed
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, an invalid COMMENTS_STORAGE_BACKEND, a placeholder
admin secret, or a non-numeric TTL would all pass unnoticed and fail
deep inside request handling instead.

Add app/lib/env-schema.ts: a Zod schema that validates the *format* of
whatever variables are present (absolute http(s) URLs, emails, connection
URLs, the storage-backend enum, strong non-placeholder secrets, positive
integer TTL, Resend key prefix). Wire validateEnvSchema() into the
existing validateEnv() bootstrap so it fails fast in production and warns
in dev/test. Promote zod to an explicit dependency.

Adds 6 unit tests (valid set, invalid URL, invalid enum, placeholder
secret, dev-does-not-throw, unset-optional). 43/43 tests pass; tsc clean.

perf(middleware): scope matcher to documents and API, skip static assets

The middleware had no `config.matcher`, so Next.js ran it on every request
— including _next/static chunks, optimized images, fonts and other public
assets — generating a fresh CSP nonce and running the env-bootstrap import
each time. None of those static responses need a per-request nonce.

Add a matcher that excludes build output (_next/static, _next/image), the
root metadata files (favicon, robots.txt, sitemap*.xml, site.webmanifest)
and common static asset extensions, while still covering all page/document
and API routes that must carry the security headers.

Verified: production build compiles and the matcher is emitted into
middleware-manifest.json; 37/37 tests pass; tsc clean.

security(P1): reject unverifiable cross-origin mutations (CSRF)

validateRequestOrigin previously returned "allowed" whenever a request
carried neither an Origin nor a Referer header, so a state-changing POST
(contact form, comment submission) with both headers stripped bypassed
the same-origin allowlist entirely.

Fix: for mutating methods (non GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) in production, require at
least one of Origin/Referer and reject when both are absent. Safe methods
and non-production environments (local dev, tests, server-to-server tools)
are unaffected, preserving existing developer and CI workflows.

Adds regression tests covering: allowed/blocked Origin, allowed/blocked
Referer, Referer-only success, the new no-headers production rejection,
the non-production allowance, safe-method allowance, plus characterization
tests for verifyTurnstileToken (test short-circuit, fail-closed on missing
secret, token-required in prod). 37/37 tests pass; tsc clean.

ci: add activation note to relocated secret-scan workflow

Bot lacks GitHub App 'workflows' permission, so the gitleaks workflow
ships in .github/pending-workflows/. A repo owner must move it to
.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml to activate it (one git mv).

test(env): commit placeholder-only .env.test template

Allow-list .env.test in .gitignore and commit it. It contains ONLY safe
placeholders and Cloudflare official test keys (no real secrets, verified
by gitleaks), so CI and contributors can run `npm test` without access to
production credentials.

test(env): decouple test suite from real secrets file

Point the test script at the committed, placeholder-only `.env.test`
instead of the gitignored `.env.local` (which holds real production
secrets). Allow override via DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH for local debugging.

All 25 tests pass against `.env.test` (Cloudflare official test keys +
safe placeholders); tests set their own env values internally, so no
real secret is required to run them.

security(P0): remediate committed secrets and DB artifacts

Security-incident remediation only. No functional/refactor changes.

- Untrack .env.local (real production secrets) — file kept on disk, now
  gitignored so it can never be re-committed.
- Untrack SQLite runtime artifacts (auto-comments_database_url-3ngrfn
  {,-shm,-wal}) — build/runtime output, kept on disk, now gitignored.
- Harden .gitignore: database artifacts (*.db/-wal/-shm/*.sqlite*, data/*)
  and env variants (.env.*, keep only .env.example).
- Sanitize .env.example: replace the real leaked Cloudflare Turnstile
  secret (hash-identical to .env.local) and remove its duplicate; use
  Cloudflare official TEST keys and documented placeholders; fix Redis
  port (3000 -> 6379).
- Add gitleaks config (.gitleaks.toml) with project detectors for
  Turnstile / Resend / comments-admin-token / DB+Redis DSNs, allowlisting
  documented placeholders and the gitignored .env.local.
- Add Secret Scan CI workflow (gitleaks on push/PR/weekly).

NOTE: exposed secrets in prior history are purged in a subsequent history
rewrite; the values must be rotated out-of-band (owner action, confirmed).
